title: Navigation Aids, Anchors, Sensory Cues & Counterplay
objective: Implement navigation/anchor bindings; governed law responses to aids; anomaly cue grammar and accessibility-equivalent cue contracts; MCS/MSAS/presentation handoffs; counterplay provenance and owner-operation routing; and the owner-approved local-frame, anchor and breadcrumb navigation model that does not assume a universal global compass.
acceptance: Navigation aids can bind to explicit local frames, anchors and breadcrumbs rather than assuming one global compass.
Aid responses are governed spatial-law responses routed through existing owner operations and never mutate law truth directly.
Anchors and breadcrumbs preserve provenance and canonical owner references across frame changes.
Anomaly cue grammar has semantic/nonvisual and keyboard-equivalent representations for every blocking cue.
MCS/MSAS/presentation handoffs project authorized cue/navigation state without owning canonical spatial truth.
Counterplay operations preserve owner authority, permission filtering and immutable Event provenance.
Navigation aids do not reveal hidden topology, undiscovered identifications or protected predicates beyond MSLR-04 authorized knowledge.
Blocking navigation/counterplay workflows remain provider-off and paid-cloud independent.
boundaries: MSLR-01/03/04/07/08 and upstream completed programs remain sealed.
Canonical topology, metric law and frame state remain owned by their existing MSLR runtime contracts.
Knowledge/Visibility owners retain authorized participant discovery and hidden-topology filtering.
MCS/MSAS/presentation systems remain projection/cue owners rather than spatial-truth owners.
GPR/Action/Event retain generic execution and immutable Event history.
MSLR-14 and later tranches remain unauthorized until MSLR-13 closeout.
next_action: Await the next owner Continue. That command may governed-start only amended MSLR-13.
